newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Masood ready for conditional ceasefire--spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Masood ready for conditional ceasefire--spokesman.

text.p: The ousted government of Afghanistan said on Monday it was ready to sign a ceasefire agreement with the Taleban militia but only on condition that the capital Kabul would be "demilitarised".
"If a ceasefire is agreed today, then talks on the demilitarisation of Kabul should start immediately," said Dr Abdullah (one name), spokesman for the government's top commander, Ahmad Shah Masood.

Taleban sources said Babar had flown back to the Dostum-held northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif from Kandahar on Monday to transmit the Taleban's response to the offer of a ceasefire due to take effect from midday (0730 GMT).

Haqqani said the Taleban wanted the truce to be monitored by a 12-man commission, six from the Taleban and six from opposed factions, including those of Dostum, ousted government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood and Shi'ite Moslem leader Karim Khalili.
If the ceasefire held, and prisoners were exchanged, peace talks could follow, Haqqani said.
Babar has been shuttling between Kandahar and Mazar-i-Sharif to try to prevent fighting between the Taleban, who captured Kabul on September 27, and Dostum's Uzbek forces.
